name: Return Path Checker
blurb: return-path problems of layer changes and the stitching vias they need
intro: Pick the situation a trace is in: the table says what its return current does and the fix. For layer changes it sizes the return via or capacitor so the via loop stays under 10 % of the trace impedance at the edge's knee frequency (0.5 / rise time), and gives the λ/20 stitching pitch.

inputs.label: Situation
options: Layer change around one shared plane
Layer change: GND plane to another GND plane
Layer change: between two power rails
Trace over a slot / merged anti-pads
Trace near the plane or board edge
Through a connector / to another board

inputs.label: Signal via to return via / cap

examples.title: USB 2.0 HS pair dropping from L1 to L6 (GND to GND), 1.6 mm board
SPI clock moving to a PWR-referenced layer

usage: Pick the scenario (same-plane, gnd-gnd, gnd-pwr, pwr-pwr, split, slot, edge, connector, no-plane) and give the rise time in ns and εr; for layer changes also the trace impedance (Ω), board thickness, via drill and via-to-return distance (mm) and the number of signal vias. It returns the knee frequency, the λ/20 stitching-via pitch, the via loop inductance and reactance, the largest distance for the return via or capacitor, how many are needed, and the fix for the case. Use it when reviewing layer changes, plane splits and board edges.
sources: H. Johnson, M. Graham, High-Speed Digital Design, Prentice Hall 1993, 1.1 (knee frequency 0.5/tr)
C. R. Paul, Inductance: Loop and Partial, Wiley 2010, ch. 5 (two-wire loop inductance)
H. W. Ott, Electromagnetic Compatibility Engineering, Wiley 2009, ch. 16 (return paths, split planes, stitching)
E. Bogatin, Signal and Power Integrity - Simplified, 3rd ed., ch. 10; λ/20 stitching pitch and 10 % of Z0 are rules of thumb
